title: SPELLZ: MY EXPERIMENT WITH CLAUDE
author: Dacrikka
selftext:
Hi all! I'm Edo, an Italian creative director. I use ComfyUI and local models for my job, and i wanted to push myself forward by creating a video game with the assistance of Claude Opus/Sonnet.  
The game is Spellz, a turn-based wizard duel that runs in the browser (smartphone/PC as well).   
I generated 500+ images on one RTX 5070 Ti and 159 went into the game. No cloud credits.

Base setup:  
• Model: Krea2 turbo (krea2\_turbo\_fp8\_scaled)  
• Text encoder: qwen3vl\_4b, type krea2  
• VAE: qwen\_image\_vae  
• Sampler: er\_sde, simple scheduler, 8 steps, CFG 1.0  
• Negative: ConditioningZeroOut  
• Style LoRA: DnDPainterlyKrea2Raw at 0.8  
• Kids Edition: same graph, Niji\_Sweet\_Spot\_Krea2\_v2A at 0.7

Keeping the same graph and only changing the LoRA gave me two different art directions from one pipeline.

Batch through the API: I did not queue the assets by hand. A Python script holds every asset as a job (name, size, batch count, prompt), sends the graph to /prompt, polls /history and downloads from /view. Claude Code wrote these scripts.

Sprites with clean alpha: I generate on flat magenta (255,0,255) and key it outside ComfyUI with numpy:

1. Estimate the real background color from the median of the four corners.
2. Measure how much background chroma each pixel has, on both R-G and B-G. Red leaves stay opaque because their B-G is negative.
3. Build a soft alpha, erode it 1 px and blur it a little.
4. Unmix the foreground color: F = (C - (1-a)\*bg) / a
5. Remove the leftover magenta spill.

Purple objects need a safe mode: only pixels almost identical to the background become transparent, so violet crystals are not lost.

Seamless ground: I blend each texture with a copy shifted by half its size, using a smoothstep mask near the edges. Then I check a 2x2 preview for visible joins.

What I learned about prompts:  
• “Game ground texture” gave me full scenes with rocks. “Flat square texture swatch, extreme close-up looking straight down” gave me usable ground.  
• Negative phrases inside the positive prompt (“no ground, no cast shadow”) helped keep sprites clean, even with CFG 1.  
• Sprites are exported at 2x and drawn at 0.5 scale, so they stay sharp on phones.

The last step is manual. I chose every image from contact sheets, then fixed the assets by hand in Photoshop and Krita. A beautiful image is not yet a game asset.

The game is free to play here: [https://dacrikka.itch.io/spellz](https://dacrikka.itch.io/spellz)

Here my complete process: [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4AwGiQlUXI](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=M4AwGiQlUXI)

Hope you likre it!
